questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: From the start I knew that I wanted to do my exchange in Spain, but I chose to do it in Madrid because I have a lot of connections there, plus its a big city with a lot of travel opportunities, you can easily take the train a couple of hours and go to other cities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I love Madrid, it has been the coolest place to study, but the way they teach their clases has been a little difficult for me, because of the lack of dialogue in class between teacher and student, which is something that I've been used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was very simple actually, they send you emails and information all the time, and once I got to the university everyone was helpful if I needed to know anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really need any assistance other than the first day when I needed to find the Erasmus office, or when I needed to find out how to print, but that was it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were three girls looking for an apartment to share, so it wasn't that difficult, we found an apartment in Lavapiés through "Spot a home".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It obviously is much more expensive to live off campus, especially if you are by yourself in Madrid. Other than that, the metro and busses takes you everywhere, so you don't really have to worry about the distance between your home and campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of paperwork, and they were very slow to accept and sign my "forhåndsgodkendelse".

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Once you get to your host institution they send you a lot of documents you have to sign, and you have to make your schedule by yourself, make sure that the courses don't overlap each other, and then you just show up to your chosen courses, you also have to get each teachers signatures to show that they have accepted your assistance in their classes. 
Once you have all the signatures you have to go to the Erasmus office and get the faculties stamp and get registrated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office helps you with everything you have to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful, the only difficult thing was to make sure you don't overlap your courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of paperwork, so be prepared to have a little patience.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall i was very pleased with my courses, besides this one course where the teacher wasn't that structured and it was very frustrating.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses have different groups, some for first year students, second and so on, I mostly took courses for the first year students because I didn't know a whole lot about the subjects, other than I wanted and was interested in learning more.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I didn't like the way they teach that much, the clases was an hour and a half long without the usual 15 minutes of break that we get in UCPH, so it was hard to focus especially when the teachers just talk and talk the entire time, I missed a little more dialogue between student and teacher. 
Also, the fact that I chose first year courses also meant that the other student were very young and unserious in class, there wasn't a mutual student/teacher relationship of respect. 
In UCPH we are used to be treated as the adults we are, and the clases are much more respectful. In UCPH its your own responsibility to pass the courses, but its not mandatory to assist to the classes, in UCM you could suspend if you don't show up.
Another thing was the amount of "homework" you get if you choose to do the "continuous evaluation".

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I chose 4 courses in "La facultad de ciencias de la información", and one in "La Facultad de Filología"

Facultad de ciencias de la información:
- Pragmática y discurso en el Periodismo
- Teoría de la Comunicación
- Historia del Pensamiento Político Contemporáneo
- Ciencia Política y Relaciones internacionales

Facultad de Filología
- Lingüística y Estudios Culturales

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed Teoría de la Comunicación and the way my teacher Fransisco Javier Malagon Terron, teaches his class.
Also Pragmática y discurso en el Periodismo, Raquel Taranilla García, was my best Teacher during this exchange.
Both of these courses were very instructive.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Unexpected sickness, medicine costs for example

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The transportation costs were less than I expected, if you are a student you can travel in all Madrid for 8 euros per month, all you want.
Restaurants were more expensive than I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: With the campus card and your Erasmus card, you have access and offers to most social activities, outdoor pools and fitness centers, the campus also has a lot of different sports teams you can join if you wish.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely join the campus fitness or other sport teams, and take advantage of the offers they provide in museums and clubs as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel out of Madrid, Toledo for example, as I said earlier, with the train from Madrid you can basically go everywhere so easily.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me it was very easy because I have family and friends in Madrid already, so I've been here a lot. I love this city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open, people are very open to do things together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The healthcare system, it was very frustrating to go to the doctor, they take and eternity and I felt like they didn't take me seriously.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The atmosphere, Madrid just have a good vibe in general, the fact that people are so relaxed and social.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient 
Take advantage of the offers you get with the campus card 
Sit in the front of the class, to make sure you are able to hear what the teacher is saying.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always ask your professors for help if there's anything you have doubts about, they are always ready to help

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Once you get used to the metro you feel like a local, and free to go anywhere.
Also when you pass your courses obviously.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Medical attendance, but that's it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy and have fun in everything your doing during your exchange, time flies by so fast.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
